subject: Pilot: short-run runway — bridging fee vs prorated seat swap
messages:
From: Ash Patel <ash@cloudbridge.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Quick ask — 3-week runway top-up or seat swap?

Hi Neha,

Quick note from our side: we’re seeing the pilot burn a bit faster than expected on our extraction flows. The engineers would like an extra 3 weeks to finish the connector and run a second validation pass.

Two things we wanted to ask:
- Is there a short "bridging fee" option to add 3 weeks to the existing pilot?
- Alternatively, can we convert unused pilot hours into prorated seats (so we can keep the team running while we finish work) and apply a credit toward a committed seat package if we convert?

We’d rather avoid a full amendment if possible. Procurement will need a stub (scope + price) to approve. Attaching rough usage numbers below.

Would appreciate a quick call or a short note with options. Thanks — we’re close to a conversion and want to avoid losing momentum.

—Ash
Ash Patel
Head of AI Infrastructure
CloudBridge AI
(attachment: pilot_usage_snapshot.csv)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ash Patel <ash@cloudbridge.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 3-week runway top-up or seat swap?

Hi Ash — thanks for the clear ask and the usage snapshot. We can definitely do something lightweight without a full contract amendment. Two pragmatic options we commonly offer:

1) Bridge add-on (simple one-off fee)
- Add 3 weeks to the current pilot. One-time bridging fee equal to 20% of the remaining pilot list value (covers priority capacity and a small engineering uplift). No change to license terms.
- Fast approval path: we provide a one-page amendment (DocuSign) and invoice net 30.

2) Prorated seat swap + conversion credit
- Convert remaining pilot token-hours into N prorated developer seats for the duration of the extra run (we’ll calculate using actual burn rate).
- If you convert to a 12+ month Dedicated/Committed seats within 30 days, we’ll apply a conversion credit equal to the pro-rated value of the swapped hours.
- Requires a short addendum but we can do a streamlined playbook flow (no legal redline expected).

I’ve cc’d David for the technical sizing and Marissa for commercial confirmation. David — can you confirm the seat count estimate given the attached usage? Marissa — can you confirm we’re ok to offer the conversion credit against a 12-month commit?

If both sound ok to you, I’ll draft the short amendment and share a one-pager for procurement. If you prefer, we can also do a quick 20-minute call this afternoon.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ash Patel <ash@cloudbridge.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 3-week runway top-up or seat swap?

On Thu, Sep 10, 2026 at 11:32 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> I’ve cc’d David for the technical sizing and Marissa for commercial confirmation.

Thanks — looked through Ash’s usage file and ran a quick projection. Two notes:
- Given the current mix (heavy vectorization + long-context LLM runs), 3 weeks of runway will map to roughly 4 prorated developer seats (8–10 users with staggered activity) if you choose the seat swap.
- The bridging fee approach is cheapest for a pure short runway; the seat swap gives you continuity for engineers but requires a follow-up conversion decision.

I attached a short calc (bridging_fee_calc.xlsx) with the numbers I used — it’s a simple multiplier on burn rate and priority capacity. No hidden costs.

Happy to sync on specifics if you want me on the call.

—David
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: bridging_fee_calc.xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ash Patel <ash@cloudbridge.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 3-week runway top-up or seat swap?

Hi Ash — quick commercial confirmation from my side:

We can authorize both options to move quickly:
- Option A (Bridge): approve the one-off bridging fee at 18–22% band depending on final usage rounding. We’ll target 20% as Neha suggested.
- Option B (Seat swap): approve prorated seat conversion plus a conversion credit equal to the pro-rated pilot value if CloudBridge signs a 12-month committed seat agreement within 30 days of the pilot end.

To make procurement happy, I’ll share our standard one-page amendment and a short pricing playbook excerpt. If procurement needs it, we can also add a clause that the conversion credit applies only to subscription fees (not professional services).

Attachment: redwood_pricing_playbook.pdf (excerpt).

Neha — feel free to send the DocuSign amendment; keep the bridge fee number provisional until David confirms final hours.

—Marissa
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Ash Patel <ash@cloudbridge.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudbridge.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick ask — 3-week runway top-up or seat swap?

Hi team — thanks, that all looks good. We prefer Option B (prorated seat swap) to keep the team productive. Procurement asked for two items before they sign off:
1) A one-page amendment or SOW showing the seat count, effective dates, and the conversion credit language.
2) A billing stub (one-off invoice amount) for internal approval routing.

If you can send both today we’ll route through procurement and legal. I’ve cc’d procurement on this thread.

Appreciate the quick turnaround; we aim to finish the connector and flip to a committed seat purchase by mid-October.

—Ash
Head of AI Infrastructure | CloudBridge AI

- Generate a billing stub/invoice for the prorated value and send to procurement.

Expect both in the next 2 hours. If procurement needs any alternate billing terms, loop me in and we’ll adjust.

Thanks — we’ll get this turned around quickly.
